content:
Another week, another streaming service price hike. This week, ESPN announced that the monthly fees for both ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited will increase, and some Disney+ and Hulu bundle prices will also go up.

This price increase was spotted by Sports Media Watch via an ESPN support page. The new prices will take effect on September 17. Details are as follows:

  • ESPN Select monthly fee: $14 per month (originally $13 per month)
  • ESPN Select annual fee: $140 per year (originally $130 per year)
  • ESPN Unlimited monthly fee: $32 per month (originally $30 per month)
  • ESPN Unlimited annual fee: $320 per year (originally $300 per year)

As reported, since ESPN revamped its streaming strategy last year, this is the first price increase for these services.

At the same time, some Disney-related bundles will also see monthly fee increases in line with ESPN streaming price hikes.

  • Disney+ (with ads), Hulu (with ads), and ESPN Select: $22 per month (originally $20 per month)
  • Disney+ (without ads), Hulu (without ads), and ESPN Select: $33 per month (originally $30 per month)

As The Verge noted, this price increase also affects the legacy no-ads Hulu, Disney+, and ESPN Select bundle, which is no longer accepting new subscribers. The monthly fee will increase from $25 to $28.

The good news: the ESPN Unlimited bundles are not affected by this adjustment.

Peacock also announced price increases last week, up to $3 more per month or $30 more per year. Apple has also recently raised prices for Apple Music and Apple One.

My favorite Apple deals right now:

  • AirPods Pro 3: $190 (originally $249)
  • AirTag 2: starting at $20 each (originally $29)
  • M5 Pro MacBook Pro: $2,699 (originally $3,199)
  • AirPods Max 2: $429 (originally $549)
  • Apple Watch Series 11: $329 (originally $429)
